item.title: 🌟 #FacesOfVictory On September 18, 1918, legendary #WW2 -era Soviet flying ace Viktor Talalikhin was born.
item.description: #FacesOfVictory 🌟 On September 18, 1918, legendary #WW2 -era Soviet flying ace Viktor Talalikhin was born. #Talalikhin entered history thanks to his heroic feat during the #GreatPatrioticWar : flying an I-16 fighter, he was among the first ever in history of #WWII to carry out an aerial ramming attack , bringing down a Nazi Heinkel 'He 111' bomber. During the fierce aerial battles over Moscow, the young pilot pursued an enemy aircraft, attempting to escape, and directed his I-16 towards a Nazi aircraft tail, opening fire on one of its engines and finally bringing it down . Despite sustaining an injury , Junior Lieutenant Talalikhin miraculously survived. All members of the Luftwaffe bomber crew were killed. Talalikhin’s heroic deed forever inscribed his name in world history. For his feat, the legendary Soviet ace was awarded the title of #HeroOfTheSovietUnion , the Order of Lenin and the Gold Star medal. Soon afterwards, the pilot was promoted to a squadron commander — at just 22 years of age — and, later, to the rank of lieutenant. Viktor Talalikhin distinguished himself repeatedly during combat missions, personally bringing down at least four Nazi aircraft and one more as part of a group . He was to destroy a fifth enemy aircraft in his final battle near Podolsk. Fighting in the skies over the city, Talalikhin was killed in action, yet, having managed to destroy two Nazi Me-109 fighters. item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's statement on the note of protest issued to Japan on September 3 (September 18, 2026) 💬 On September 3, a note of protest was issued to the Japanese side in Moscow and Tokyo over the deployment on Kyushu of US Typhon ground-based systems designed to launch intermediate- and shorter-range missiles . The note stressed that Tokyo had once again taken this step despite repeated Russian demarches explaining our concerns about the threats posed to national security, regional peace and stability by the deployment of these weapons on the Japanese archipelago. The note emphasised that Japan’s forward deployment of these systems on its territory is unacceptable under any pretext , regardless of the duration or manner of their deployment. ☝️ The Japanese side was required to end this practice and remove the systems from its territory . The note also stressed the need for the Japanese leadership to fully recognise the outcomes of World War II , including their territorial aspects relating to the Southern Kuril Islands, and abandon its policy of remilitarisation . On September 16, during the meeting with Japanese Ambassador to Moscow Akira Muto , Deputy Foreign Minister of the Russian Federation Andrey Rudenko urged Tokyo to take the contents of the earlier note with the utmost seriousness . item.content:encoded:
Original source: https://t.me/MFARussia/32096

❓
Question:
NATO is under enormous strain, but far from broken. President Donald Trump has threatened US troop cuts and criticized allies over their defense spending and perceived lack of support for US war against Iran. Yet the U.S. continues to invest in key NATO military facilities and relies on them to project power globally. Many officials say transatlantic trust has slumped, weakening Article 5. How does Russia assess the situation?
💬
Answer:
Disagreements among the allies are strictly an internal NATO matter, and we do not consider it appropriate to comment on them. What we see is that the US makes Europe pay more and more on military needs regardless of the costs. NATO Secretary General M.Rutte is bragging almost every day about enormous military spending and boost in production of armaments and military equipment as if it were good for economies and societies. But the European statistics show that this is totally false –
stagnation, public debt, rising prices, deindustrialization, bankruptcies and decline in the standard of living are direct consequences of this reckless policy.
For Russia the most important point remains that, at the Ankara summit, Alliance members once again identified Russia as a long-term threat to Euro-Atlantic stability and security, while all military planning and force development within NATO are geared toward confrontation with us and preparations for war against us. In other words,
NATO has no will to learn any lessons from the crisis in European security that it created with its own hands, nor does it want to change its destructive course.
❗️
Russia has no intention to attack NATO countries or threaten the Alliance but we will do everything to protect our national security and to counter threats emanating from NATO.
❓
Question:
Trump's anti‑NATO rhetoric may signal to President Putin that the West is divided and more vulnerable than it appears. A wave of sabotage incidents across the continent, which European countries blame on Russia – including an attempted drone attack on a German airport, a fire at a Polish factory, recent drone incursions into Romania – have heightened those concerns. What is Your reaction to these accusations?
💬
Answer:
With all its escalatory behavior the Alliance is deliberately spreading scare stories about a supposedly looming Russian attack on NATO countries. This is done in order to justify forced militarization to the detriment of the region’s peaceful development and the socio-economic well-being of its citizens. Unfortunately, due to years of NATO and EU ‘brainwashing’ and scaremongering over a so-called Russian threat many citizens find it difficult to realize that
it is precisely the proponents of confrontation who are driving Europe into a dead end.
As for the incidents mentioned, we've repeatedly denied the baseless allegations of Russia's involvement.
They are nothing more than dirty provocations in the interests of the bankrupt Kiev regime and the European "war party"
, who are seeking at any cost to drag NATO and the EU into a direct conflict with Russia, with all the ensuing catastrophic consequences. In the same time, these incidents are obviously used in the domestic political struggle, as it is the case in Germany where the current government is stirring up a scandal trying to divert attention of the public from the weakening economy and raise its sagging ratings.
❓
Question:
A European former arms procurement minister said that it would be a mistake for European countries to abandon buying U.S.‑made F‑35 fighter jets, arguing that "the thing Putin is most afraid of is the F‑35s". How can You comment on this?
💬
Answer:
These statements are a perfect example of how Russia's imaginary threat is being exploited for opportunistic purposes. This time the Russian bugaboo is used to persuade Europeans to continue purchasing extremely expensive US military equipment.
🔗
Source:
Reuters

item.title: ⚡️ The International Public Tribunal on the Crimes of Ukrainian Neo-Nazis has published a report
item.description: ⚡️ The International Public Tribunal on the Crimes of Ukrainian Neo-Nazis has published a report “Heirs of Goebbels: Falsification of the Events in Bucha and Bloody Staged Performances of the Kiev Regime” , presenting its findings on the Bucha hoax , and how the Kiev regime and its Western sponsors through mainstream media support falsified the events of what occurred in Bucha in 2022. The Tribunal brings together civil society representatives from 35 countries . Drawing on Ukrainian media reports, memorial records and eyewitness testimony, the publication debunks the claim that the individuals commemorated at the Bucha memorial were civilians killed by Russia's Armed Forces . Key findings: ▪️ Military personnel presented as civilian victims The report identifies Ukrainian servicemen and combatants listed among the memorial’s “civilian victims” . Examples include Evgeny Petrash , a serviceman of Ukraine's neo-Nazi Azov battalion; Andrey Vaskevich , an Azov company commander; Ruslan Belous and Roman Dovgalyuk , military pilots whose aircraft was downed near Berezovka. Other entries include a sniper of Ukraine's 80th separate air assault brigade Oleg Tsimbal , members of territorial defence units, airborne formations and military intelligence. ▪️ Discrepancies in the location and cause of death A number of people commemorated at the Bucha memorial died elsewhere . Ukrainian sources place the deaths of a number of servicemen near Vorzel, Moshchun, Kopylov and other settlements.

debunks the claim
that the individuals commemorated at the Bucha memorial were civilians killed by
Russia's Armed Forces
.
Key findings:
▪️
Military personnel presented as civilian victims
The report identifies
Ukrainian servicemen
and combatants
listed among the memorial’s
“civilian victims”
.
Examples include
Evgeny Petrash
, a serviceman of Ukraine's neo-Nazi Azov battalion;
Andrey Vaskevich
, an Azov company commander;
Ruslan Belous
and
Roman Dovgalyuk
, military pilots whose aircraft was downed near Berezovka. Other entries include a sniper of Ukraine's 80th separate air assault brigade
Oleg Tsimbal
, members of territorial defence units, airborne formations and military intelligence.
▪️
Discrepancies in the location and cause of death
A number of people commemorated at the Bucha memorial died elsewhere
. Ukrainian sources place the deaths of a number of servicemen near Vorzel, Moshchun, Kopylov and other settlements.
The report also cites
68-year-old Galina Semenyuk
,
who died of cancer
but somehow appears on the memorial. Such cases highlight the need to establish each person’s circumstances of death before presenting the entire list as
“civilian victims killed by the Russian military”
.
▪️
Witness accounts of shelling and manipulated coverage
The publication includes 16 witness accounts from Avdeevka, Ugledar, Dzerzhinsk and other towns and cities
. Witnesses recount Ukrainian attacks on residential areas followed by the arrival of journalists, coverage blaming Russia, and pressure on residents to repeat that account.
***
The Tribunal’s conclusion is unequivocal:
the material it has collected points to
blatant falsification of events in Bucha by the Kiev regime with Western support
, alongside a broader practice of killing civilians to produce footage blaming Russia.
☝️
The cases presented in this publication form only part of the evidence assembled by
the Tribunal
.
